raw_case_text:
We present a 39-year-old heterosexual man with a pertinent past medical history of well-controlled HIV on HAART, including dolutegravir, lamivudine, and abacavir, and atovaquone prophylaxis and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis. Atovaquone prophylaxis, 750 mg PO every 12 hours, was initiated 5 months prior when the patient was first diagnosed with HIV with CD4 count 81 cells/muL and acute renal failure. The patient first presented to the hospital for evaluation of shortness of breath. During this admission, computerized axial tomography (CT) chest demonstrated interstitial lung disease with ground glass opacities and intrathoracic lymphadenopathy (Figures 1 and 2). The patient underwent bronchoscopy, which was suboptimal due to technical difficulties. Transbronchial biopsies, bronchoalveolar lavage, and cytology were inconclusive. Furthermore, acid-fast bacilli (AFB) cultures were negative. Unfortunately, the patient declined VATS. In addition, the patient had significant peripheral eosinophilia 11.8% (ref.: 0.0-6.0) and occasional urine eosinophils (ref.: negative). At this time, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia was not suspected due to normal CD4 count 487 cells/muL with atovaquone prophylaxis and HIV RNA <20 copies/mL. Other diagnosis considerations included iatrogenic-induced subacute hypersensitivity pneumonitis and sarcoidosis. Abacavir was switched to rilpivirine due to suspicion of hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and the patient was discharged on 40 milligrams prednisone daily, and atovaquone prophylaxis was continued due to prednisone therapy. Following these treatments, there was both a radiographic and clinic response. The patient received a twenty-four-day course of prednisone. Follow-up CT chest demonstrated persistent, extensive bilateral ground glass opacities and improved mediastinal lymphadenopathy (Figure 3).
The patient presented back to the hospital ten days after discontinuation of prednisone for evaluation of worsening shortness of breath, malaise, and fever. On presentation, the patient was hypoxic (oxygen saturation 88% on room air), febrile (38.8 C), tachycardic (heart rate low 100 s), and tachypneic (29 breaths per minute). Physical exam was remarkable for increased work of breathing and diffuse bilateral rales.
Repeat CT scan showed substantially worsened diffuse bilateral ground glass and more dense airspace consolidations (Figure 4). A bronchoscopy with right VATS and lung biopsy was performed. Cytology was negative for malignancy, and AFB stain was negative. Grocott's methenamine silver stain of pathology from right upper, middle, and lower lobe resulted positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii.
The patient's atovaquone for PCP prophylaxis was discontinued, and renally dosed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg/day (trimethoprim component) IV was initiated. The patient was discharged on 2 tablets of oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (160-800 mg tablet) daily for a total course of twenty-one days, in addition to a short course of prednisone. The patient experienced significant relief of shortness of breath following completion of trimethoprim-sulfamethazine course and prednisone taper. PCP prophylaxis was changed to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (80-400 mg) three times a week after dialysis. The patient has not had recurrence of respiratory complaints since completion of treatment for PCP and is expected to complete a 12-month minimum course of trimethoprim-sulfamethazine prophylaxis in September 2019.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old heterosexual man with well-controlled HIV and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented with worsening shortness of breath, malaise, and fever 10 days after completing a 24-day course of oral prednisone despite ongoing atovaquone prophylaxis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV and acute renal failure 5 months earlier (initial CD4 count 81 cells/μL), the patient was started on dolutegravir, lamivudine, abacavir, maintenance hemodialysis, and prophylactic oral atovaquone (750 mg PO q12h), achieving immune recovery (CD4 487 cells/μL, HIV RNA <20 copies/mL). He first presented with shortness of breath, ground-glass opacities and intrathoracic lymphadenopathy on chest CT, peripheral eosinophilia (11.8%), and urine eosinophils; after a technically suboptimal bronchoscopy, abacavir was switched to rilpivirine for suspected drug-induced hypersensitivity pneumonitis and he completed a 24-day course of oral prednisone (40 mg daily) while continuing atovaquone prophylaxis. Ten days after stopping prednisone, he re-presented with acute worsening shortness of breath, malaise, and high fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed 5 months prior (well controlled with CD4 487 cells/μL and HIV RNA <20 copies/mL on dolutegravir, lamivudine, and rilpivirine); end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis; recent 24-day course of oral prednisone (40 mg/day) for suspected abacavir hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening shortness of breath, malaise, and fever at readmission. Home medications were dolutegravir, lamivudine, rilpivirine, and prophylactic oral atovaquone (750 mg PO q12h).

objective.physical_examination: Readmission vital signs: Hypoxemic with SpO2 88% on room air, febrile at 38.8 °C, tachycardic (heart rate in the low 100s beats/min), and tachypneic (respiratory rate 29 breaths/min). Physical exam: Increased work of breathing and diffuse bilateral rales on lung auscultation.
objective.routine_investigations: First admission labs: Peripheral blood eosinophilia of 11.8% (reference: 0.0%–6.0%), occasional urine eosinophils, HIV RNA <20 copies/mL, and negative AFB cultures.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunological status at first admission: Recovered CD4+ T-cell count of 487 cells/μL (up from 81 cells/μL at diagnosis 5 months prior). Serial chest CT scans: First admission CT showed bilateral ground-glass opacities and intrathoracic lymphadenopathy (mediastinal adenopathy improved after prednisone, but GGOs persisted); readmission CT demonstrated substantially worsened diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities and dense airspace consolidations. Readmission bronchoscopy and right video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) wedge biopsies of the right upper, middle, and lower lobes: Negative for malignancy and AFB; Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) staining of lung biopsy tissue from all three right lung lobes was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Breakthrough Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) in a virologically suppressed HIV-positive hemodialysis patient with a normal CD4+ T-cell count (487 cells/μL) receiving oral atovaquone prophylaxis (750 mg BID), unmasked/precipitated by a 24-day course of oral prednisone (40 mg/day) and definitively confirmed by Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) staining on right upper, middle, and lower lobe VATS lung biopsies. Plan and clinical course: Atovaquone was discontinued, and the patient was treated with renally dosed intravenous trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (5 mg/kg/day TMP component) transitioned at discharge to oral TMP-SMX (two 160/800 mg tablets daily to complete a 21-day course) plus a short oral prednisone taper. His dyspnea resolved completely, and he remained recurrence-free on thrice-weekly post-dialysis TMP-SMX prophylaxis (80/400 mg).
